quotes.text: Artificial Intelligence has its benefits, but there is also potential for serious harm that we are now experiencing with several investigations in South Dakota. That harm is real with ‘deepfakes’ that include the use of real children’s voices and photographs taken from social media to create computer generated child porn.

As Attorney General, I fully support the State’s ability to impose reasonable regulations on AI within South Dakota. AI has its benefits, but left unchecked, it could lead to real dangers to the public ranging from explicit material and election interference to deception, exploitation, and harassment against consumers.
I believe the South Dakota legislature should look at the opportunity to limit or prohibit the use of AI to do deepfakes and what a candidate is saying or doing, or those election filings

I’m a strong supporter of AI, I think it’s great innovation. I’m an electrical engineer. There are a lot of positive things can happen with it. I use it as a law enforcement tool to help victims and further investigations. [...] So the three areas that we want to see guardrails on and protection on are the pornography side, the election integrity side, and for consumers.
Whether as attorney general or a member of Congress, my position will be local control. Some communities don't want it; it should not be forced upon them.

My position is, if a data center is going to come in, there has to be adequate power. I would support requiring it to be a positive on the grid, so that if a data center comes in, they have to add to the grid so that it doesn't affect the available supply of electricity and the ultimate cost of electricity.

We're in a race right now with AI with China, and we need to win that race. AI has, and I'm speaking as an electrical engineer, has wonderful opportunities to help businesses, make them more efficient, develop education. There need to be guidelines.

What we did in Meta with respect to protecting online safety with kids and what we do with AI is better put in legislation. It's better decided in a legislative debate rather than a courtroom. But we need to have action with respect to furthering AI and its development with respect to China, but putting guardrails in place to protect the public.
